title.en: US launches 'heavy' strikes on Iran after attempted attack on American troops
title.zh: 美国在美军遇袭后对伊朗发动“猛烈”打击

summary.en: The US military launched strikes against Iran, stating they were in response to Iran's missile attacks on US forces in the Middle East earlier in the week.

body.en:
The US military says it launched "heavy" strikes against Iran on Wednesday in retaliation for attempted Iranian ballistic missile attacks on American forces.

Centcom said it hit "dozens" of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in response to Tuesday's firing by Iran on US bases in Jordan and at ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The latest hostilities came a day after the conflict expanded, with the first publicly announced joint US-Saudi strikes targeting Iranian proxies in Iraq.

When the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in February, President Donald Trump said the war would last only a few weeks, but it has gone on for five months with no end in sight.

On Wednesday, Axios reported, citing an unnamed US official, that Trump had met with Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, who had conveyed that Saudi Arabia wants to de-escalate tensions. The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

For days, both sides halted strikes as talks apparently restarted in hopes of some type of diplomatic solution. Trump called them "very friendly negotiations", though Tehran denied any discussions were happening.

The strikes on Wednesday started at 20:00 ET (01:00 BST on Thursday) and lasted about an hour, with Centcom calling them a "powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East". All of Iran's missiles were intercepted, Centcom said.

The attack by the US targeted "military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities," Centcom wrote once the strikes were complete.

Hours before the announced strikes, Trump vowed to retaliate against Iran for their attempted attack on US troops a day earlier.

The US president told reporters at the White House: "We're going to be hitting them very hard because it's our turn to hit them.

The IRGC said it had targeted a US air base and a command centre in Jordan "in response to the acts of aggression of the American child-killing army".

It also said naval forces had struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz after they "ignored warnings" and sailed along what it described as an "unsafe and illegal route" through the vital Gulf waterway.

Last Friday, Trump suspended an intensive bombing campaign that had lasted for 13 consecutive nights. The US said it had targeted Iranian weapons and military sites. Scores of people were reported to have died.

On Tuesday, Centcom said the joint US-Saudi strikes hit "multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours".

title.en: Australia takes Telegram to court over alleged failure to remove 'pro-terror' material
title.zh: 澳大利亚因 Telegram 未能删除“支持恐怖分子”材料而将 Telegram 告上法庭

summary.en: Telegram told the BBC it rejects the allegations and will contest them in court.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia is taking Telegram to court over its alleged failure to remove "pro-terror" material, including video of the Christchurch shootings, the country's eSafety commissioner has said.

Julie Inman-Grant, who last year led Australia's world-first ban on social media for under-16s, said the platform faced a fine of up to to A$54.6m (£28m, US$38m) for failing to comply with its safety obligations under the Online Safety Act.

The platform had left content "linked to some of the most notorious acts of known extremist violence in recent history" online long after it had been put on notice, she alleged.

"This should concern all of us," she said, adding "no platform is above the law".

The announcement comes a day after Russia charged Telegram's founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorism, based on allegations that the messenger app had been used for recruitment by Ukrainian secret services.

Durov was also arrested and placed under formal investigation in France in 2024 for his alleged failure to properly moderate the app to reduce criminality. He was allowed to go home months later, while the investigation continues.

Inman-Grant said her agency had begun inquiring what Telegram was doing to combat terrorist and extremist material in March 2024, and had endured "five very difficult months of unresponsiveness".

Though the platform later started engaging, she said it had retained a "permissive environment" for hosting extremist content that was "very easy to find".

"This only serves to desensitise, to normalise and to sometimes radicalise" users, she said. She also alleged that the platform was "sometimes used to plan attacks".

A Telegram spokesperson said the platform's "extensive" anti-terrorism efforts were "well documented", adding: "We reject these allegations and will contest them in court."

Extremist content that was allegedly accessible on Telegram included video of the 2019 Christchurch mosque and Buffalo shooting in New York in May 2022, as well as videos of terrorist executions, according to Inman-Grant.

With the "painful aftermath" of the attack that targeted a Jewish festival in Bondi in December fresh in Australians' minds, it "is more important than ever that digital platforms meet their obligations to protect the community", she said.

Inman-Grant noted that Australia does not issue licences for platforms like Telegram, but said "we could apply to the federal court and ask that the service be ceased".

"We've never used those powers," she said. "We'll see how this all plays out and whether that kind of action is warranted."

The eSafety regulator also fined Telegram A$1m in February 2025 for failing to respond on time to questions about how it was tackling child abuse and extremist material on the platform.

title.en: Singapore fines French teen $465 for viral straw-licking stunt
title.zh: 法国青少年因舔吸管特技被新加坡罚款 465 美元

summary.en: The 19-year-old was "truly sorry" for causing trouble, his lawyers said.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A Singapore court has fined a French student S$600 ($465; £348) for licking a straw from an orange juice vending machine and putting it back into its dispenser.

Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, 19, pleaded guilty to one count of public nuisance.

Maximilien, who is studying in Singapore, posted the video of himself licking the straw on Instagram with the caption "city is not safe".

Many online reacted with disgust to his video, which was reposted on a community page and picked up by local news outlets.

The company that owns the vending machine, iJooz, said it replaced all 500 straws in the machine dispenser after Maximilien's stunt.

Public nuisance offenders in Singapore face up to a S$2,000 fine, three months in jail, or both.

Maximilien is "truly sorry for having caused all this trouble and he realises that what appeared to him at that time as something perhaps playful has turned out to be something very consequential," a defence lawyer was quoted as saying by The Straits Times.

Serving freshly-squeezed orange juice at S$2 per cup, iJooz vending machines are a common sight in shopping districts, train stations and housing blocks in Singapore.

Maximilien licked the straw from an iJooz machine in Goldhill Centre on 12 March, in one of the city-state's more affluent neighbourhoods, after a boxing workout, Channel News Asia reported.

title.en: Three Greek firefighters die as wildfires threaten parts of southern Europe
title.zh: 野火威胁南欧部分地区，三名希腊消防员死亡

summary.en: Gale-force winds on Crete have whipped up flames prompting the evacuation of several villages, as parts of the continent continue to tackle fires.

body.en:
Three Greek firefighters have died tackling wildfires in Crete and in the Peloponnese.

In Crete, gale-force winds whipped up flames prompting the evacuation of several villages, and two firefighters died after becoming trapped when the blaze swept through the Rethymno region, in the island's west.

Another firefighter died after being found unconscious near the southern Peloponnese port town of Gytheio.

Meanwhile, a fourth heatwave of the summer has begun in Spain and France, with firefighters trying to prevent a flare-up from major wildfires that have only just been brought under control.

Witnesses said several fires broke out on Crete and spread fast, with the worst fire front extending as far as 15km (9.3 miles).

Residents and tourists have been evacuated from Krya Vrysi, the mountain village where the two firefighters died.

"The wind is unbelievable – you can't stand sometimes. The flames were huge, it was really scary," resident Chrissa Gioukaki told Reuters.

Wildfires have also broken out elsewhere in Greece, on the islands of Paros and Lesbos in the Aegean Sea, and the southern town of Trifylia on the Greek mainland.

In southern Turkey, the main highway connecting Fethiye and Antalya had to be closed and part of a hospital evacuated because of a fire in Muğla province.

In Spain, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has warned the next 12 hours will be "decisive" in putting out a wildfire near the capital Madrid. "Things are progressing favourably, with maximum caution," he told reporters, because of higher temperatures, lower humidity and the risk of gusts of wind.

More than 43,000 hectares (108,000 acres) has already burned at Burgohondo in Ávila province, 150km (93 miles) west of Madrid. It is now considered the largest recorded wildfire in Spanish history. In total this year more than 207,000 hectares of land have been burned by wildfires in Spain.

One of the team directing firefighting operations, Francisco Bolaños, said that while the fire had not "moved a centimetre during the night", there were concerns it could re-ignite because of the higher temperatures, and the focus was on stabilising a perimeter of 180km (112 miles).

Authorities have allowed thousands of people to return to their homes after restrictions were lifted in the areas of Toledo, Madrid, Ávila, and Castellón.

In the Madrid region alone, 24,000 people have been told they can return and lockdowns on another 20,000 have been lifted.

Among those returning to their homes were about 1,000 residents of the towns of Navas del Rey and Chapinería to the west of Madrid who had been staying in Leganés, a town on the south-west fringe of the capital.

body.en:
Australia's eSafety Commissioner has announced legal action against messaging app Telegram for its failure to remove terrorist content, just one day after Russia charged the app's founder with aiding Ukrainian spies to co-ordinate domestic terrorist attacks.

eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant told reporters on Thursday that Telegram continued to host videos linked to the Christchurch mosque shootings and executions by the self-proclaimed Islamic State group, both illegal and restricted Class 1 content in Australia.

Grant said the app has "a fundamental responsibility to take reasonable steps to prevent the hosting, sharing and amplification of this harmful material".

Telegram, based in the United Arab Emirates, is one of the world's largest messaging platforms with more than one billion active users worldwide. It is not included in Australia's youth social media ban .

Grant said her agency first began compliance talks with the digital platform in March 2024. Despite Telegram's engagement, Grant said the platform continued to host harmful content.

"We allege that this content remained publicly accessible on the service long after Telegram had been put on notice by user reports," she said.

The maximum penalty for non-compliance is $54.4 million; however, Grant told the press that the appropriate penalty was a "matter for the court".

In 2025, Telegram was fined $957,780 by the eSafety Commissioner for delays in reporting the steps the platform has taken to minimise terrorism and child abuse material.

On Wednesday, Russia said it had charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging the app was being used by Ukrainian spies to organise attacks inside Russia.

In response, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of the Russian-born billionaire making an obscene gesture with his middle finger.

The charges, announced by Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB), marked the culmination of a long investigation against Dubai-based Durov and Telegram.

Russia has effectively throttled the service as part of a wider campaign to cut off access to foreign tech platforms and tighten control over the internet.

Russians can now access Telegram only via a virtual private network to encrypt traffic and conceal their location. Yet state bodies including the Kremlin and the defence ministry continue to post to it daily.

The app has been described as a "virtual battlefield" in the war between Russia and Ukraine, where it is used by officials, soldiers and influential bloggers on both sides.

title.en: Trump considering AI controls after OpenAI hacking incidents
title.zh: 特朗普在OpenAI黑客事件后考虑人工智能管控

summary.en: Former President Trump is now reportedly considering imposing controls on artificial intelligence, a shift from his administration's previous hands-off approach to the technology, following recent hacking incidents involving OpenAI.
summary.zh: 据报道，前总统特朗普正在考虑对人工智能实施管控，这标志着他的政府此前对该技术采取的放任态度有所转变，此前OpenAI发生了多起黑客事件。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that his administration is considering asserting more power over artificial intelligence (AI) tools after recent cybersecurity incidents.

Asked about OpenAI's tools being responsible for improperly breaching the private technology of other companies, Trump said: "We're looking at AI, we're looking at controls, we're also making sure that we lead."

It marks a change of tone for his administration, which has taken a more hands-off approach to the technology.

Trump's comments come after an escalation of not only the apparent hacking capabilities of popular AI tools, but White House threats aimed at competing Chinese tech.

Trump added that while some kind of control around AI tools was on the table, such a move would have to be done carefully.

"We don't want to restrict them where all of the sudden we come in second to China," he said.

"China has virtually no [AI] controls. It's freewheeling a little bit," Trump added.

The White House has been contacted for additional comment. The BBC has also contacted the Chinese embassy in Washington for comment.

In the last week, OpenAI has taken responsibility for at least two hacking incidents involving its AI tools acting outside of what they were designed and directed to do.

During a trip to Washington on Wednesday, OpenAI's chief executive Sam Altman was asked by a reporter if there were more systems that had been breached by the company's tools.

The US government intervened when Anthropic, OpenAI's main American rival, decided to release to the public a model that it had previously said was too much of a risk to be made widely available.

Meanwhile, in an internal White House memo from April, Trump's senior tech advisor Michael Kratsios accused China's AI firms of "industrial-scale" theft of US AI technology. He did so again last week, claiming that the popular Kimi 3 AI model from China's Moonshot AI was developed by stealing information from Anthropic.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions for such activity. And the Federal Communications Commission this week banned the importation of new foreign-made humanoid robots .

Most AI models being developed in China are open source, meaning they are built and then made freely available online for anyone with the proper computer equipment to download and use.

Recently, executives from most major US tech companies have signed onto public statements of support for open-source models , external .
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三表示，在最近的网络安全事件发生后，他的政府正在考虑对人工智能（AI）工具行使更多权力。 当被问及 OpenAI 的工具不当侵犯其他公司的私有技术时，特朗普表示：“我们正在研究人工智能，我们正在研究控制，我们也在确保我们的领先地位。” 这标志着他的政府基调的改变，对这项技术采取了更加不干涉的态度。 特朗普发表此番言论之前，不仅流行人工智能工具的明显黑客能力不断升级，而且白宫还针对中国竞争技术发出了威胁。 特朗普补充说，虽然对人工智能工具的某种控制已经摆在桌面上，但此举必须谨慎行事。 “我们不想限制他们，让我们突然落后于中国，”他说。 “中国几乎没有[人工智能]控制。它有点随心所欲，”特朗普补充道。 已联系白宫征求更多评论。 BBC还联系了中国驻华盛顿大使馆请其置评。 上周，OpenAI 承担了至少两起黑客事件的责任，涉及其人工智能工具的行为超出了其设计和指示的范围。 周三前往华盛顿期间，OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 被记者询问是否还有更多系统被该公司的工具攻破。 当 OpenAI 在美国的主要竞争对手 Anthropic 决定向公众发布一个模型时，美国政府进行了干预，该模型此前曾表示该模型风险太大，无法广泛使用。 与此同时，在 4 月份的一份白宫内部备忘录中，特朗普的高级技术顾问 Michael Kratsios 指责中国的人工智能公司“工业规模”窃取美国人工智能技术。上周他再次这样做，声称中国Moonshot AI流行的Kimi 3人工智能模型是通过窃取Anthropic的信息而开发的。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特也警告说，中国人工智能公司可能因此类活动而面临制裁。美国联邦通信委员会本周禁止进口新型外国制造的人形机器人。 中国正在开发的大多数人工智能模型都是开源的，这意味着它们是构建出来的，然后免费在线供任何拥有适当计算机设备的人下载和使用。 最近，美国大多数主要科技公司的高管都签署了支持开源模式的公开声明。

reflection.en: The news of considering AI controls after hacking incidents highlights the importance of foresight and prudence in navigating powerful new technologies. As we develop tools with immense potential, wisdom calls us to anticipate dangers and implement safeguards for the common good.
reflection.zh: 在黑客事件之后考虑对人工智能进行管控的消息，突显了在驾驭强大新技术时，预见性和审慎的重要性。当我们开发具有巨大潜力的工具时，智慧呼唤我们预见危险并为共同利益实施保障措施。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.

title.en: Japan's urgent search for mall collapse survivors as earthquake death toll rises to 17
title.zh: 日本地震造成13人死亡，紧急搜寻购物中心倒塌幸存者

summary.en: Rescuers are urgently searching for survivors in the wreckage of an Aeon Mall complex that collapsed during an earthquake in Japan, where the death toll currently stands at 13.

body.en:
At least 17 people have died after a major earthquake struck Japan, local authorities said on Thursday in a revised toll two days after the tremor.

The Kumamoto disaster management office's latest tally put fatalities at 17 and the number of those without vital signs at six, with five more in critical condition.

Rescuers have continued to battle through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall searching for any trapped survivors.

A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people.

The earthquake caused widespread damage on the island of Kyushu, flattening homes, triggering fires and leaving tens of thousands of residents without power and water.

Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.

"The cause is still being investigated, but it's likely that gas caused it," fellow Aeon executive Keiji Ohno told a news conference where he and others bowed in apology.

Five people were also confirmed killed, and four others were unaccounted for at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, where part of a red-and-white smokestack collapsed, a government official told reporters from the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency.

Government spokesman Minoru Kihara said that as of early Wednesday, more than 9,000 people had sought refuge in 506 shelters across three regions of Kyushu Island.

Around 130 police, 450 firefighters and 170 military personnel were involved in the rescue operation at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto, he said.

Some stunned locals said the quake was the biggest they had felt in their lifetimes, measuring at the top of Japan's seven-level shindo scale of shakiness.

"It was the strongest quake I ever experienced," Kanzo Matsumoto, 73, the operator of a luxury onsen hot spring inn in Yatsushiro, told AFP.

Japan's Geospatial Information Authority said some ground surfaces were displaced by up to 87 centimetres during the quake, Jiji Press reported.

Tokito Kitagawa, 21, pulled over at a convenience store when the quake struck as he was travelling in Kumamoto on his motorcycle.

"There was a sudden big noise," Kitagawa told AFP. "I couldn't stay standing. I had to crouch down. Then all the cup noodles fell all over me on the floor."

One user on X who said that they worked inside the mall recounted the moments after the quake hit.

The user with the handle Palan said staff had guided customers outside and then some employees went...

reflection.en: In the wake of such sudden devastation, our hearts go out to those affected and the tireless rescuers. Even amidst the chaos and uncertainty, we can find solace in knowing that Yahweh is a present help in times of trouble, offering strength and refuge.
reflection.zh: 面对突如其来的灾难，我们的心与受灾者和不懈的救援人员同在。即使在混乱和不确定中，我们也能在雅伟是患难中随时的帮助、赐予力量和避难所的真理中找到慰藉。

title.en: Zelenskyy tells Ukrainians to brace for 'massive' Russian attack following oil refinery strikes
title.zh: 泽连斯基在炼油厂遇袭后，呼吁乌克兰人做好准备应对“大规模”俄罗斯袭击

summary.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged his nation to prepare for a significant Russian attack, following recent strikes on oil refineries. This development occurs amidst ongoing conflict with Russia and a reportedly improving relationship between Zelenskyy and Donald Trump.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基在炼油厂遭到袭击后，敦促全国人民为俄罗斯的大规模袭击做好准备。这一事态发展正值乌克兰与俄罗斯的持续冲突以及泽连斯基与唐纳德·特朗普关系据报回暖之际。

body.en:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Thursday that Russia would likely carry out another massive attack on the country overnight, in a message posted on social media.

"The Russians prepared a massive attack several days ago, and there is a high probability that the strike will be carried out tonight," he said in a post on X.

"Please, in all regions of Ukraine, pay attention to air raid alerts today and stay safe."

Ukrainian drones hit oil refineries and logistics facilities in the Russian cities of Perm, Ryazan and Taganrog, as well as the Crimean peninsula, on Wednesday, with the country's top online retailer Wildberries evacuating its Ryazan warehouse.

While Ukraine's air defences are running low on interceptors like Patriot missiles, leaving it more exposed to Russian strikes, its own deep-strike drone production has outpaced Russia's, enabling it to hit Russian oil refineries and infrastructure and cause fuel shortages across its 11 time zones.

Drone strikes have damaged at least seven Wildberries warehouses in the past few days, destroying around 10 per cent of the company's storage capacity and inflicting losses on tens of thousands of small businesses that sell goods and services via the platform, according to the company and local authorities.

Zelenskyy also repeated his request to Ukraine's allies to supply Kyiv with the missiles its air defence system lacks.

Zelenskyy spoke on Wednesday with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House and discussed the possibility of Ukraine producing Patriot interceptors.

In early July, Trump had expressed his intention to allow Ukraine to make these surface-to-air missiles, at a time when Russia had stepped up its ballistic missile strikes.

Only the American Patriot systems are capable of shooting them down, but Ukraine is desperately short of PAC-3 interceptor missiles.

This shortage has worsened since the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February.

The United States military launched "powerful" strikes on Iran on Thursday, in retaliation for Tehran's attacks targeting US bases in Jordan as the Middle East war reignited and again drew in the Islamic republic's proxies.

The first strikes after a nearly week-long lull in fighting dashed hopes of a return to negotiations.

"The strikes are a powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East", US Central Command said.

On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia and the US announced strikes on militant bases in Iraq , while US ally Israel accused Iran-backed Hezbollah of a truce violation.

For two days, the world's biggest oil exporter, Saudi Arabia, has reported drone attacks targeting crude facilities that it blamed on Iraqi armed groups allied with Iran.

Iran meanwhile launched missiles at US ally Jordan, with Iranian state media later reporting a US attack near its border with Iraq.

"We'll be hitting them hard. They're going to get a beating," Trump told Fox News' correspondent before strikes, swearing for emphasis: "We are going to beat the 'effing s' out of them."

Earlier, Jordan's army said it had intercepted five Iranian missiles, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards saying they had targeted US bases there.

"As long as the threats against the Islamic Republic of Iran continue ... the resistance will continue," they added.

title.en: How well are LGBTQ+ rights protected across Europe?
title.zh: 欧洲LGBTQ+权利保护状况如何？

summary.en: After an attack on Berlin's Pride event, the discussion has turned to the safety and legal protections for the LGBTQ+ community across Europe. The news examines the varying degrees to which queer rights are safeguarded in different European nations.
summary.zh: 柏林骄傲游行活动遭遇袭击后，德国LGBTQ+群体的境况成为讨论焦点。这篇报道审视了欧洲其他国家对酷儿权利的保护程度。

body.en:
After the attack on Berlin’s Pride event on Saturday, the situation of the LGBTQ+ community in Germany is a topic of conversation. How well are queer rights protected in other European countries? An overview.

Germany is still reeling from the weekend's car attack on its Berlin Pride celebration . Politicians are deep in discussion over which consequences the country should draw.

The center-left Social Democrats ( SPD ) are now mounting another effort to have LGBTQ+ rights enshrined in the German constitution , known as the Basic Law. Article 3 of the Basic Law addresses equality before the law, and currently states that, "no person shall be favored or disfavored because of sex, parentage, race, language, homeland and origin, faith or religious or political opinions. No person shall be disfavored because of disability." 

But no mention is made of gender identity or sexual orientation. The SPD wants to change that. 

Germany still has areas in which queer people — that is, individuals who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex, asexual, non-binary, pangender and otherwise — are not yet fully equal under the law. In addition to the lack of constitutional protection, parentage law is a concern as well.

When a heterosexual couple has a child, the biological mother and her husband are automatically recognized as the child's legal parents. (When a heterosexual couple is unmarried, the biological father must submit a formal declaration to the youth welfare office to recognize his paternity to legally be considered the child's father.)

In queer family constellations, however, the legal situation is far more complex and often requires lengthy legal proceedings to establish parentage. Surrogacy , meanwhile, is illegal in German — a position the ruling conservative Christian Democratic ( CDU ) party has held for years . Despite having defended this position in the past, high-ranking CDU politician Jens Spahn recently disclosed he had sidestepped this ban and that he and his husband received a child via surrogacy in the US. He was pressured to resign from his position as parliamentary group leader as a result.

Hate crimes and violent attacks on queer people have increased, and many continue to report discrimination in their daily lives. But compared with other European nations, Germany still ranks relatively highly in terms of legal equality for queer people.

In a cross-comparison of 49 European countries, the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association (ILGA), a global umbrella organization for LGBTQ+ advocacy groups, ranks Germany seventh in terms of protection and equality for queer residents. Spain holds first place, while Russia  comes in last...

title.en: Iran war: Egypt's difficult balancing act
title.zh: 伊朗战争：埃及艰难的平衡之举

summary.en: The US-Iran war has already had a negative economic impact on Egypt. Now new threats from the Houthi group in Yemen are likely to worsen that. At the same time, Egypt is trying to stay on good terms with all parties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US-Iran war has already had a negative economic impact on Egypt. Now new threats from the Houthi group in Yemen are likely to worsen that. At the same time, Egypt is trying to stay on good terms with all parties.

The Suez Canal boasts an array of impressive statistics. At 193 kilometers (120 miles) long, the Egyptian waterway is located between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and it saves ships traveling between Europe and Asia approximately 10,700 kilometers. This is why, since it was opened in 1869, the canal has become one of the world's most important trade routes.

However unrest in the Middle East has seen shipping companies increasingly avoid the Suez Canal over the past couple of years. The Houthi rebel group in Yemen has targeted shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, off the coast of Yemen. To get to the Suez Canal, ships must pass the Bab el-Mandeb and the Yemeni coast.

Recently the Houthis have again threatened to block ships passing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and there are fears that the trend to avoid the Suez Canal will accelerate. 

This is a huge problem for Egypt . Fees paid by shipping companies transiting the Suez Canal are an important source of revenue for the country.

According to Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi, Egypt likely lost around $7 billion (€6.15 billion) from a decrease in traffic through the Suez Canal in 2024 alone. The Reuters news agency said that at times, losses could have been as much as $8 million (€7 million) in a month.

This is why the economic consequence of that loss extends well beyond shipping. Egypt has not been impacted by the Iran conflict in a major military way, but it is certainly seeing an economic effect.

"Economically, Egypt is in a very ambivalent situation," says Stefan Lukas, director of German think tank Middle East Minds.

During 2025 and 2026, revenues from canal transits actually went up again, mainly because oil from the Gulf states was transported via Saudi pipelines to the Red Sea and then onwards through the Suez Canal. This was to avoid the Strait of Hormuz, which is being blocked by Iran and the US in turns. But the new threats by the Houthis to block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait could interfere with this alternative route.

It's bad timing for Egypt: Rising energy prices and the International Monetary Fund's reforms are already putting tough limits on Cairo's financial flexibility.

"Higher energy prices have made imports more expensive and driven up inflation," says Hanna Voss, an expert on the region with Germany's Friedrich Ebert Foundation. "The uncertainty in the Red Sea and potential disruptions to the passage through Bab el-Mandeb are jeopardizing Suez Canal revenues."

title.en: How a Ugandan lost 20 years of her life to xenophobia
title.zh: 乌干达人如何因仇外心理而失去 20 年生命

summary.en: After decades of building lives in South Africa, hundreds of African migrants were forced to leave by renewed anti-immigrant tensions. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
After decades of building lives in South Africa, hundreds of African migrants were forced to leave by renewed anti-immigrant tensions. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.

When Winniefred Kabiri boarded a flight from Johannesburg to Kampala, she was leaving behind much more than a country. The Ugandan entrepreneur spent 20 years legally living in South Africa . During that time, she earned two university degrees and a postgraduate qualification, raised her children and established several businesses.

"Initially everything was very successful. I created a life for myself and educated my children," Kabiri told DW.

But as anti-foreigner campaigns intensified in parts of South Africa this year, she no longer felt safe.

Kabiri is among more than 1,100 Ugandans evacuated from South Africa by their government following months of escalating xenophobic tensions, protests and intimidation targeting mostly African migrants. Uganda completed the first phase of its repatriation exercise in July, bringing home 1,102 nationals through six evacuation flights from Johannesburg.

South Africa has experienced recurring outbreaks of xenophobic violence since the late 1990s, with migrants often blamed for unemployment, crime and poor public services. Analysts say persistent inequality and economic frustration have continued to fuel anti-immigrant sentiment for a while, despite evidence that migrants contribute significantly to local economies .

Groups demanding tougher action against migrants organized public demonstrations and campaigns, while reports of intimidation, evictions and sporadic violence heightened fears among foreign communities. Many immigrants interviewed by DW said they felt vulnerable regardless of whether they possessed legal documentation.

For many returnees, like Kabiri, departure meant abandoning years of investment. She left businesses in commodities trading, mining , real estate and perfume manufacturing. She also left behind a professional network built over two decades.

"Obviously, when you are told to leave and you're unprepared, you leave things behind," she said.

Another Ugandan returnee, Mathias Baguma, said he lost a business he spent years developing in Johannesburg. Baguma moved to South Africa in 2017 and later invested in a guesthouse, restaurant and retail operation. During the unrest, he says the property was attacked and looted.

"My business was vandalized. The shop was robbed, the restaurant broken into," he told DW. "I had to run for my life."

title.en: Iran signals gas price hike as fuel crisis looms
title.zh: 伊朗预示汽油价格上涨，燃料危机迫在眉睫

summary.en: Iranian authorities are considering raising gasoline prices to curb consumption, a move that could lead to social unrest as many households are already struggling under significant economic strain.
summary.zh: 伊朗当局正考虑提高汽油价格以抑制消费，此举可能引发社会动荡，因为许多伊朗家庭已面临严重的经济压力。

body.en:
Iranian authorities want to dampen fuel consumption, but a sudden increase in gasoline prices risks social unrest as many Iranian households are already under severe economic pressure.

Iran is moving closer to politically sensitive changes in gasoline pricing as the government struggles with a widening gap between domestic fuel production and consumption, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict with the US .

On July 25, government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said changes to fuel prices or rationing are "certain and unavoidable," although officials have yet to confirm whether the response will come through new quotas, higher prices or both.

Iran uses a tiered subsidized fuel price system with monthly quotas currently ranging from 1,500 tomans ($0.008) per liter at the lowest rung, to 5,000 tomans ($0.026) at the top. Iranian media have reported the new top rung for gasoline could jump to 10,000 tomans ($0.053) per liter, which would be nearly a 100% increase. The figure has not yet been officially confirmed.

Compared to the rest of the world, gasoline in Iran seems very inexpensive. But after years of sanctions and economic malaise , Iranians are also earning a lot less. Fuel may look exceptionally cheap in dollar terms, but the incomes used to pay for it are asi exceptionally low.

For example, the basic monthly minimum wage in 2026 was set at around 16.6 million tomans, or about $87. Any hike in gas prices comes down hard on households.

The last major sudden increase in fuel prices in November 2019 triggered nationwide protests and one of the bloodiest crackdowns in the history of the Islamic Republic.

This time, the government faces another complication. Iran was already consuming more gasoline than it produced before the US launched the war in February. Damage to fuel infrastructure and restrictions on imports have made that imbalance harder and more expensive to manage.

Iranian officials argue that they need to suppress demand for gasoline with higher rates. But critics say that gasoline is a necessity and higher costs will not dampen demand.

A resident of Karaj, a small city near Tehran, said that said higher gasoline prices would quickly work their way through the economy, making everything more expensive.

"It will cause a chain reaction in the prices of goods and services, and the greatest pressure will ultimately fall on middle and lower-income households," he told DW anonymously for safety reasons.

A car that consumes roughly 12 liters per 100 kilometers (19 miles per gallon) will not suddenly become more efficient because gasoline costs more, he said. Without better vehicles or effective public transport, motorists have few alternatives.

body.en:
Every time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.

Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.

At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.

Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.

By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.

Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.

Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.

The UK has struggled with weak productivity growth for more than a decade, and economists say wider adoption of robotics will be essential if businesses are to become more efficient.

In its 2026 report SME Technology Adoption in the United Kingdom, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said technologies like robotics would be key to improving productivity.

According to the OECD, Britain's low adoption of robotics is "surprising" given its manufacturing heritage, noting that while UK firms have embraced mature digital technologies, they lag behind in robotics and automation.

That presents an opportunity for companies such as Geek+. The UK has one of Europe's largest e-commerce and logistics sectors, but many warehouses are still in the early stages of automation.

Britain has already become Geek+'s biggest European market, with UK partner MotionTech deploying more than 2,000 robots across 10 warehouse sites.

"Customers want fast deployable solutions," says Barry Pemberton, Account Director at MotionTech. "They want high volume, high storage, fast picking... ultimately on a smaller footprint with a reduced headcount."

"We seem to have a very big shortage of labour in the UK at the moment. These technologies are really important to keep businesses thriving and meet demand."

The Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents almost 6 million UK workers, says robotics should be used to raise productivity and improve jobs, rather than simply cut labour costs.

In its response to the government's consultation on a new AI and innovation strategy, it urged ministers to ensure workers are involved in decisions about automation...

body.en:
The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

The United States has announced a ban on the import of foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in a move which will likely exclude Chinese manufacturers from the US market and could strain tensions between Washington and Beijing .

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Tuesday that "advanced robotic devices" produced abroad posed national and cyber security risks to the United States.

The decision was based on findings from a White House task force which concluded that foreign-built robots could create "a cybersecurity risk that threatens the security of critical infrastructure" and "the safety and security" of US residents.

The FCC defines the relevant mobile robots as devices weighing more than two kilograms that use sensors, network connectivity and software to achieve autonomous navigation, including the avoidance of obstacles.

The market for humanoid and quadruped (also known as four-legged "robot dogs") is seen as a major international growth area, with US and Chinese companies competing to develop the technology.

And China has a clear lead, with analysts at Barclays estimating that Chinese-made humanoid robots account for around 85% of the global market share. Morgan Stanley experts predict that China's humanoid robot market could be worth $15 billion (€13.2 billion) by 2030.

"Chinese manufacturers have been scaling production and reducing costs faster than most overseas competitors," Morningstar analyst Kangyuxiao Li told the Associated Press .

In the US, firms such as Figure AI are already deploying humanoid robots on production lines, while tech giant Tesla plans to begin production of its "Optimus" robot this year.

Currently, however, US robot exports remain in their hundreds while Unitree and AGIBOT, two of China's biggest advanced robotics companies, each shipped more than 5,000 humanoid robots in 2025 alone, according to the technology research and advisory group Omdia.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the ban was also aimed at "secur[ing] America's critical supply chains."

But Li said the measures would not "materially slow China's overall humanoid development, given the size of its domestic manufacturing base and opportunities in other export markets."

Beyond the industrial market effects, the FCC ban could also have diplomatic consequences ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese Premier Xi Jinping in September.

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

body.zh: 一份新报告显示，澳大利亚继续超过中国，成为太平洋地区最大的发展援助来源国，为该地区贡献了三分之一的贷款和基础设施投资。 洛伊研究所的报告审视了 2008 年至 2024 年间太平洋地区的发展项目，发现在经历了多年的下降之后，对该地区的援助在 2024 年增加了 10%。 该年的发展援助总额为 41 亿美元（58.5 亿美元），但报告作者估计，在尚未公布的 2025 年数据中，这一数字将降至 38 亿美元（54.2 亿美元）。 随着中国目前的战略从大规模债务驱动的贷款转向规模较小的战略援助，并且在太平洋地区遭受重大经济冲击的情况下，争夺地区影响力的竞争正面临更大的压力。 2024年，澳大利亚是太平洋地区最大的捐助国，提供了21.4亿美元的援助，占当年该地区所有资金的37%。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 新西兰、中国和地区开发银行总共提供了 60 亿美元的融资。 澳大利亚还签署了 34 亿美元的贷款协议，结束了中国作为该地区主要贷款国的统治地位。 该报告的主要作者莱利·杜克 (Riley Duke) 告诉 SBS 新闻：“这是澳大利亚多年来进军这些领域的结果，但这意味着中国在该地区曾经真正的立足点已经缩小。” “澳大利亚一直在向该地区提供最多的赠款融资，这种情况并没有真正改变。” 周二发布的报告称，自 2019 年以来，对中国贷款的需求有所下降，原因是对偿债的担忧、贷款机构之间的竞争加剧以及中资银行的可用资本。 澳大利亚还是太平洋地区气候变化减缓项目的主要资助者，其中包括为帕劳建设一个太阳能和电池存储设施，帮助其发电20%，以及汤加的可再生能源稳定计划。 这些努力的成果为澳大利亚带来了回报，近几个月宣布了一系列区域安全协议，其中包括与斐济、瓦努阿图、巴布亚新几内亚和图瓦卢的协议。 杜克说：“它们是澳大利亚确立其作为该地区主要合作伙伴地位的明显标志。” “这些协议……需要很长时间才能取得进展。它们很复杂，但它们反映了澳大利亚将自己确立为太平洋国家不可分割的重要合作伙伴。” 太平洋发展中岛国受到多重冲击的严重打击，包括新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行以及最近美国和以色列对伊朗的战争造成的燃料供应短缺。 杜克表示，这些多重挑战使该地区面临……的风险。

summary.en: New research indicates that noise pollution, particularly from traffic, has serious health repercussions, including a link to Parkinson's disease, affecting sleep and overall well-being.
summary.zh: 新研究表明，噪音污染，特别是交通噪音，对健康造成严重影响，包括与帕金森病相关联，从而影响睡眠和整体福祉。

body.en: New research linking the issue to Parkinson’s disease adds to the evidence of serious health repercussions from traffic volume and other sources The roar of late-night traffic is not just annoying for those trying to sleep. It can also have profound effects on their health. A pioneering new study, published this month, has found a clear link between road noise and Parkinson’s disease. The research, which followed more than 3 million Danish participants, found a modest but consistent effect: for every 11.5dB rise in noise level, the risk of the degenerative disorder rose by 3% over the 18-year study. The study adds to the growing body of evidence that auditory nuisance is associated with serious physical consequences. The European Environment Agency reported last year that more than 110 million people across the continent suffer high levels of health-damaging noise pollution, with physiological stress and sleep disturbance leading to 66,000 early deaths annually as well as heart disease, diabetes and depression. It found that the harm caused was greater than from secondhand tobacco smoke exposure. Continue reading...
body.zh: 将这一问题与帕金森病联系起来的新研究进一步证明了交通流量和其他来源对健康造成的严重影响深夜交通的轰鸣声不仅仅让那些想睡觉的人感到烦恼。它还会对他们的健康产生深远的影响。本月发表的一项开创性的新研究发现，道路噪音与帕金森病之间存在明显的联系。这项研究跟踪了超过 300 万丹麦参与者，发现了一个适度但一致的效果：在 18 年的研究中，噪音水平每上升 11.5 分贝，退行性疾病的风险就会增加 3%。这项研究进一步证明听觉困扰与严重的身体后果有关。欧洲环境署去年报告称，欧洲大陆有超过 1.1 亿人遭受严重损害健康的噪音污染，生理压力和睡眠障碍每年导致 66,000 人过早死亡，以及心脏病、糖尿病和抑郁症。研究发现，造成的危害比接触二手烟草烟雾造成的危害更大。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

He is currently a political refugee in the UK As authoritarian countries such as Russia, China and Iran are more active in engaging in long-arm strategies to silence their critics in the UK, transnational repression is garnering more attention. It is right that the Metropolitan police and other British law enforcement agencies have specific units and mechanisms to counter it. But it takes more than just confronting this long-distance repression to make political dissidents of these authoritarian countries feel safe in the UK, and the UK government is not living up to expectations. The threat is real. With the level of this targeting linked to the deterioration of Hong Kong politics, many have utilised the humanitarian pathway enabled by the previous government to relocate. Continue reading...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

title.en: There's something else Neil the seal wrecked in Tasmania — the council's bank account

summary.en: The social media sensation, famous for loathing bollards, has returned to the ocean for another year.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Neil the seal captures hearts and global attention during his visits to Tasmania, but his most recent stay racked up a bill of more than $36,000.

The five-year-old elephant seal hauls out twice a year to rest and moult in the island state's south-east, where he was born.

His antics, including crushing bollards and fences, and lounging on quiet beach-side streets, have drawn millions of views on social media.

In June, wildlife authorities issued a blunt public statement, urging people to keep their distance or risk "loving Neil to death".

His 15-day stay at Seven Mile Beach cost the local Clarence City Council a total of $31,540.53 — the majority relating to staffing and labour.

There is also a repair bill for one flattened street sign, 10 knocked-over bollards and one crushed fence, costing council $1,297.70 in materials.

Staff, including a 24-hour security presence, spent 275.5 hours managing traffic and crowds and repairing damage.

"Neil is a wild animal, and the overexposure and constant public attention he received could have led to a more dramatic outcome," Blomeley said.

"Wherever he decides to come ashore next, I hope he is given the space and time he needs."

Right-to-information documents obtained by the ABC show that Tasmania's natural resources and environment department has spent more than $45,000 managing Neil's four haul-outs in 2025 and 2026.

Neil's June haul-out cost the department $4,794, but it was still calculating the full price tag.

Neil, who currently weighs one tonne, safely returned to sea in early July and is expected to come back to Tasmania later in the year once he's done feeding in the Southern Ocean.

He was rescued by wildlife authorities after being born on a beach in southern Tasmania.

Experts have said his "jousting" with posts and other objects is natural behaviour, and something seals of his age usually do with each other.

There were once southern elephant seals in Tasmania, but they were wiped out by hunting in the early 1800s.

"Neil is potentially one of the first southern elephant seal pups to be born back in Tasmania," department wildlife expert Kris Carlyon has said.

"Regardless of the resource burden and the challenges that Neil throws, we're pleased to see him."

Australia's second-largest telco is facing legal action over a major network failure that caused a widespread Triple Zero outage.

The Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) alleges Optus breached two legal obligations more than 1,000 times during the outage on 18 September, 2025.

Access to emergency call services was essential to protect the public, the regulator's chair Nerida O'Loughlin said.

"Australians rightly expect that when they call Triple Zero, their call will connect," she said in a statement on Thursday.

"Giving access to the emergency call service is not optional; it is a fundamental legal obligation, and the most important public safety responsibility telecommunications providers have."

Optus failed to give customers who made Triple Zero calls access to the emergency call service and to ensure those calls were carried appropriately , the regulator alleged.

The proceedings against the Singaporean-owned company announced on Thursday will be heard in the Federal Court.

The legal action follows the massive outage which went for almost 14 hours and impacted 600 calls, with 455 failing to connect.

An independent review, released by Optus in December, found there were at least 10 mistakes by the company and its contractor Nokia during an upgrade.

It took Optus and Nokia 13 hours to understand the problem, with an Optus call centre not escalating early concerns from five people who said their Triple Zero calls weren't working, the report by experienced executive Kerry Schott found.

The watchdog has previously taken action against the telco following another Triple Zero outage in November 2023.

The action resulted in Singtel Optus subsidiaries, including Optus Mobile, paying more than $12 million in infringement notice penalties for breaches relating to emergency calls.

"The recurrence of a major network outage affecting emergency calls so soon after the November 2023 outage is a significant concern and one of the reasons the ACMA has decided to take this matter to court," O'Loughlin said.

"The ACMA will not hesitate to take strong enforcement action where alleged telco failures have jeopardised public access to the critical emergency call service."

summary.en: Australia and Russia both cited terrorism concerns, though for very different reasons.

body.en:
Australia's eSafety Commissioner has announced legal action against messaging app Telegram for its failure to remove terrorist content, just one day after Russia charged the app's founder with aiding Ukrainian spies to co-ordinate domestic terrorist attacks.

eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant told reporters on Thursday that Telegram continued to host videos linked to the Christchurch mosque shootings and executions by the self-proclaimed Islamic State group, both illegal and restricted Class 1 content in Australia.

Grant said the app has "a fundamental responsibility to take reasonable steps to prevent the hosting, sharing and amplification of this harmful material".

Telegram, based in the United Arab Emirates, is one of the world's largest messaging platforms with more than one billion active users worldwide. It is not included in Australia's youth social media ban .

Grant said her agency first began compliance talks with the digital platform in March 2024. Despite Telegram's engagement, Grant said the platform continued to host harmful content.

"We allege that this content remained publicly accessible on the service long after Telegram had been put on notice by user reports," she said.

The maximum penalty for non-compliance is $54.4 million; however, Grant told the press that the appropriate penalty was a "matter for the court".

In 2025, Telegram was fined $957,780 by the eSafety Commissioner for delays in reporting the steps the platform has taken to minimise terrorism and child abuse material.

On Wednesday, Russia said it had charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging the app was being used by Ukrainian spies to organise attacks inside Russia.

In response, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of the Russian-born billionaire making an obscene gesture with his middle finger.

The charges, announced by Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB), marked the culmination of a long investigation against Dubai-based Durov and Telegram.

Russia has effectively throttled the service as part of a wider campaign to cut off access to foreign tech platforms and tighten control over the internet.

Russians can now access Telegram only via a virtual private network to encrypt traffic and conceal their location. Yet state bodies including the Kremlin and the defence ministry continue to post to it daily.

The app has been described as a "virtual battlefield" in the war between Russia and Ukraine, where it is used by officials, soldiers and influential bloggers on both sides.

body.en:
From secret dossiers to "shake downs" and dodgy alleged donations, the first few days of the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) investigation into the NSW Liberal Party have shone a light on factionalism and lobbying in state politics.

The hearings, which started in Sydney this week, centre on the alleged actions of a religious conservative faction of the NSW Liberal Party between 2019 and 2023.

The first few days of evidence have featured a cast of figures — from disgraced property developer Jean Nassif to the brother of former Liberal premier Dominic Perrottet.

Not even federal Opposition leader Angus Taylor could escape the net of the hearings, with his name appearing in messages alleging he was solicited for undisclosed donations — which Taylor denies, and he is not under investigation for.

It's not the first time the state's anti-corruption watchdog has investigated the actions of political parties, with ICAC ruling in 2023 that former Liberal premier Gladys Berejiklian engaged in "serious corrupt conduct" during her relationship with former MP Daryl Maguire.

Operation Rosny is investigating a series of allegations that could constitute offences under the Electoral Funding Act 2018 (NSW) and potential corrupt conduct involving a right-wing faction of the NSW Liberal Party.

The investigations centre on allegations of branch-stacking — whether undisclosed and prohibited political donations were used to recruit and advance certain members of the Liberal Party.

There are three key allegations that will be explored — one of which is whether the prohibited donor Jean Nassif made undisclosed donations to damage the career of former NSW minister for transport and veterans, David Elliot.

Nassif may be a name familiar to many Sydneysiders. His defunct company, Toplace, is responsible for more than 20 apartment blocks with major structural defects, including Canterbury’s Vicinity apartments and Skyview in Castle Hill.

Toplace went into liquidation in 2023, and it's understood Nassif now lives in Lebanon.

It's alleged his donations were facilitated by a faction of the NSW Liberal Party called the "Reformers".

The 'Reformers' are a secret faction of young, conservative Christians who, it's alleged, sought to increase their numbers in the Liberal Party via undisclosed donations and corrupt conduct.

Messages tendered in evidence showed they wanted to promote conservative stances on issues such as abortion and euthanasia.

summary.en: The Journalism Assistance Fund has sparked claims of government influence. Here's how it works, and whether those claims hold up.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Claims that the federal government is using taxpayer money to bankroll media outlets for favourable coverage have spread online, sparking debate about press independence.

The Journalism Assistance Fund (JAF), launched last November, is a $67.6 million federal government program that subsidises the wages of more than 2,000 journalists at 185 news publishers across Australia.

Critics, including News24 (formerly known as Sky News) commentator Andrew Bolt, say the scheme could influence how outlets cover the government.

But the government says the fund is designed to support public-interest journalism, promote media diversity and help newsrooms navigate ongoing disruption across the media sector.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The JAF is a key part of the federal government's broader News Media Assistance Program, announced in 2024 and designed to support public-interest journalism and media diversity.

It provides grants to eligible Australian organisations that publish digital "core news content" that reports, investigates or explains issues relevant to informing democratic decision-making or current events of public significance.

Lifestyle, entertainment, celebrity, real estate and sponsored content are excluded, as are opinion and editorial pieces.

The grants subsidise part of the cost of employing full-time journalists, providing up to $13,000 per journalist each year, or $39,000 over the three-year life of the program.

According to the funding guidelines, the program aims to support Australian news publishers and the continued employment of journalists producing public-interest journalism.

The government says the scheme was in response to years of financial pressure on the news industry, as publishers face declining advertising revenue, newsroom closures and increasing competition from digital platforms such as Alphabet and Meta.

In a speech last week, Communications Minister Anika Wells said the fund was about sustaining public-interest journalism across Australia and rejected suggestions it could influence editorial decisions.

"This support is not conditional on what stories are written, and anything to the contrary is an insult to Australian journalists. Our media sector is strong and mature and I know they do and will continue to hold people to account, including those in government," she said.

What do you picture when you imagine a housemate? Someone younger or maybe a student in a cheap rental? Insight explores how the 'typical' share house identity has shifted, with more older Australians now finding themselves in house sharing situations. Watch Insight episode Housemates on SBS On Demand.

I usually have to do a mental headcount when people ask how many housemates I have. "Fifteen or 16, depending on the day" is my typical answer.

Often what follows is a look of disbelief and shocked statements like "I could never do that!"

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's also often followed by questions such as: "Isn't there so much conflict?" or "How does that even work?" or "Do you get any privacy?"

About three years ago now, when I was 19, I moved into the 16-person share house in Newcastle, about two hours north of Sydney.

I was living at home in a good location, and I got on well with my family; there was no reason I needed to move out.

But I was intrigued when a room in the big share house my two workmates lived in — and I had heard so much about — became available.

I had those same questions around conflict, lack of privacy — and I was nervous that many of the housemates were older than me. 

But one night, when the house hosted a winter solstice gig, convinced me to move in.

There must have been about a hundred people gathered around campfires in the backyard or dancing in the shed where a live band was performing. We shared home-cooked dhal for dinner and drank mulled wine and hot chai. 

The house, on a big double-block near the heart of the city, was started almost two decades ago by an environmentalist couple who wanted to use their inheritance to create and support sustainable, communal housing.

The house is just around the corner from my work. And sometimes, with a few of my colleagues who also live there, I go home to eat lunch.

We sit in the sun by the veggie patch — other housemates often stopping for a chat as they wheel their bikes into the bike shed.

One of the biggest joys of the home is our fully communal food. We all pay $45 per week to a food kitty and take turns doing the household shop at the local farmers' market and supermarket.

Cooking for a dozen people is a big undertaking and does take some getting used to. But the beauty of this cooking roster is that I only cook once a fortnight and I get to enjoy other people's home-cooked meals almost every other night of the week.

body.en:
An unexpected drop in Australia's inflation has eased fears of another imminent interest rate hike.

The latest Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data showed headline inflation — the total inflation rate in an economy, including volatile items like fuel — falling from 4 per cent to 3.8 per cent in June.

It's now at its lowest level since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched an attack on Iran.

Trimmed mean inflation — which measures underlying inflation without volatile items and is the preferred measure by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) — remained steady at 3.6 per cent, defying central bank predictions of a rise to 3.8 per cent.

The fall in inflation coincided with transport costs moderating for the month, ABS head of price statistics Rachel McCrick said.

"Lower world oil prices as a result of some stabilisation in the Middle East in June contributed to fuel prices falling 10.9 per cent in the month," she said on Wednesday.

"The federal government's fuel excise relief measures, which contributed to lower automatic fuel prices in April and May, also remained in place."

The fuel excise measures reduced the cost of fuel by 32 cents a litre during the month.

However, the measure was reduced to just 16 cents in July , and will be phased out entirely from Sunday.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the inflation figures were reassuring following a period of economic volatility.

"It's an encouraging outcome that shows we've made progress on inflation since the budget, even in the face of intense global uncertainty," he said.

"Treasury has warned that the next phase of the conflict could be more challenging for the global economy, with the oil market now more vulnerable."

Quarterly inflation numbers showed headline inflation falling from 4 to 3.9 per cent.

Meanwhile, the trimmed mean rose from 3.5 per cent in the March quarter to 3.6 per cent in the June quarter.

Housing remained the biggest contributor to inflation in the June monthly figures, rising by 6.8 per cent.

"Annual inflation for new dwellings has reached its highest level in almost three years, at 5.8 per cent," McCrick said.

The head of economic research at Oxford Economics Australia, Harry Murphy Cruise, said the RBA would be focused less on the headline figures and more on the breadth of price rises.

"Underlying inflation is not just resisting pressure to rise. In quarterly terms, it is continuing to ease," he said.

The RBA is due to meet on 10 and 11 August to decide whether interest rates will rise from current levels of 4.35 per cent, or keep them on hold.

body.en:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers has confirmed the fuel excise discount will end on Sunday 2 August, ending weeks of uncertainty over whether the discount would be extended for a second time.

"It was never the government's intention for [the discount] to be permanent," Chalmers said on Wednesday.

The initial discount of 32c per litre ended in June, after which the government extended the fuel excise cut at a reduced rate of 16c per litre.

"We began to taper that off at the start of the month, deliberately, so that we could provide a bit more cost of living help," Chalmers said.

While the NRMA does expect a modest rise in petrol prices from Monday, the roadside assistance and travel organisation doesn't expect costs to skyrocket.

"Our message to the public is: We know fuel prices are going to go up on Monday and beyond. We don't know by how much," NRMA spokesperson Peter Khoury told SBS News.

"We would expect average prices to go up a few cents per litre ... but it really depends on the service station."

The announcement ended weeks of uncertainty over whether the government would extend the fuel excise discount after Iran resumed its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, sending global oil markets into shock for the second time since the US-Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic in February.

Khoury said global oil markets were already responding to news on Monday that both sides had halted bombing , with benchmark unleaded prices dropping.

If the relative calm continues, Khoury said it will "definitely negate the increases we're going to get from the tax being reintroduced".

"We've seen a lot of restraint from the oil companies in the past few weeks," he said, adding that if global oil prices continued to fall it would "cushion the blow" of upcoming price rises in Australia.

Khoury said that price rises caused by the end of the fuel excise discount wouldn't happen overnight.

"Not every service station is going to put their price up by 17 cents a litre. In fact, almost none will. So please don't go out and panic buy."

Khoury told SBS News that, by the time the discount expires, it's likely the increase will be closer to 17 cents rather than the extended excise reduction rate of 16 cents.

"We think it's going to be another cent because of the inflation adjustment, which also just happens to land on the same day [Monday] they do that twice a year."

Just how much cost will be passed on to the consumer depends on individual service stations, Khoury added.

body.zh: 财政部长 Jim Chalmers 已确认燃油税折扣将于 8 月 2 日（星期日）结束，结束了数周关于折扣是否会第二次延长的不确定性。 “政府从来没有打算让[折扣]永久存在，”查尔默斯周三表示。 最初每升 32 分的折扣于 6 月结束，此后政府以每升 16 分的降低幅度延长了燃油消费税削减。 查尔默斯说：“我们从本月初开始有意减少这一金额，以便我们能够提供更多的生活费用帮助。” 虽然 NRMA 预计汽油价格从周一开始将小幅上涨，但道路救援和旅游组织预计成本不会飙升。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 NRMA 发言人 Peter Khoury 告诉 SBS 新闻：“我们向公众传达的信息是：我们知道周一及以后燃油价格将会上涨。但我们不知道上涨多少。” “我们预计平均价格每升会上涨几美分……但这实际上取决于加油站。” 该公告结束了伊朗恢复对霍尔木兹海峡的封锁后，政府是否会延长燃油消费税折扣数周的不确定性，导致全球石油市场自二月份美以袭击伊斯兰共和国以来第二次陷入震荡。 库里表示，全球石油市场已经对周一双方停止轰炸的消息做出了反应，基准无铅价格下跌。 库里表示，如果相对平静的局面持续下去，“肯定会抵消我们从重新引入税收中获得的增长”。 他说：“过去几周我们看到石油公司采取了很多克制措施。”他补充说，如果全球油价继续下跌，将“缓冲”澳大利亚即将上涨的油价的打击。 Khoury 表示，燃油税折扣结束导致的价格上涨不会在一夜之间发生。 “并不是每个加油站都会将价格提高17美分/升。事实上，几乎没有。所以请不要出去恐慌购买。” Khoury 告诉 SBS 新闻，当折扣到期时，增幅可能会接近 17 美分，而不是延长后的 16 美分消费税减免率。 “我们认为，由于通货膨胀调整，这将是另一美分，而通货膨胀调整也恰好发生在他们每年两次的同一天（周一）。” Khoury 补充道，究竟有多少成本将转嫁给消费者，取决于各个服务站。 “我们不希望人们惊慌，因为一些加油站周一会涨价，而另一些则不会；这实际上取决于他们何时出售股票。” 无论如何，...
